source.title: A Scaling Law for Token Efficiency in LLM Fine-Tuning Under Fixed Compute Budgets
source.authors: Ryan Lagasse; Aidan Kierans; Avijit Ghosh; Shiri Dori-Hacohen

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the paper and appendix. Some internal reporting is inconsistent: Table 1 calls the dataset BRIMI although the text otherwise discusses BRICC, and the MMLU table's stated volumes do not match the listed mean example counts multiplied by mean token lengths.
record.tranche_reason: The study proposes a refinement to fine-tuning scaling laws and reports that data composition matters and fitted exponents vary with subsampling strategy. It does not test the original held-out pretraining-loss law.
record.gate_note: The study reports fine-tuning accuracy by subsampling strategy, normalized token-efficiency trends, a qualitative comparison with total-token scaling laws, and a statement about fitted exponents. It does not report individual fitted exponents, numerical prediction errors, or model-specific accuracy results. The BRICC/MMLU table values are aggregate summaries.
record.recipe_differences: This study fits a fine-tuning accuracy formula using dataset volume and model size, rather than measuring held-out pretraining cross-entropy against parameters, tokens, and compute. Its setup uses fixed compute and subsampling strategies; the original loss-law procedure is not reproduced.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that fitted exponents vary systematically with subsampling strategy. The study also reports accuracy differences across few long, many short, and balanced data selection.
record.problems: No individual fitted exponents, model-specific results, numerical prediction errors, or uncertainty estimates are provided. Several table and figure labels are inconsistent, and the MMLU table's reported N, L, and V values do not agree arithmetically.
record.rows_left_out: No results-bearing findings relevant to the tested versions were left out.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted to small runs.
Finding the loss-minimising parameter/token allocation at fixed compute and its scaling with compute.
Comparisons of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The study tests fine-tuning accuracy, not held-out loss; it does not test image/video modalities, repeated data, or transfer beyond the reported fine-tuning settings.
No model-specific downstream accuracy relationship with scale or pretraining loss, or quantitative test of downstream prediction from pretraining loss, is reported.
The study does not report exponent values or test parameter counting, training schedules, or alternative fitting methods; it reports exponent variation by subsampling strategy.
